angle: We ran 3 custom AI signals last month and booked 30 meetings. Here is exactly what we checked for.

risks: Sentence 29 references an on-screen reply example ('the middle reply right there'); visual context lost in audio-only clip.

angle: Everyone is using the same intent signals now. First-party signals still booked us 20 meetings last month — here is why they still win.
standalone_check: Frames the signal-commoditization problem fresh, then lands a concrete stat as proof that first-party still works.
risks: Sentences 48-49 are generic filler ('outbound is great', 'but yeah, it's great') that weaken the pacing.

angle: Skip ICP clarity and your whole signal program will fail. The five-step framework to go from zero to running custom plays.
standalone_check: Opens with a consequence that grabs attention; the next two sentences define what 'this' refers to before moving into steps.
risks: Opening 'this' refers to ICP clarity established in the sentence just before the clip; mild dangling reference resolved within two sentences.

angle: We assumed we knew our ICP. We were wrong. Here is what the closed-won data actually showed.
standalone_check: Signals upfront that there is a data surprise coming; delivers a concrete finding (product-launch correlation, fintech over-index) before the clip ends.
risks: Ends on 'right?' mid-discovery; the downstream actions taken on this finding are in later sentences not in this clip.

angle: AI mentions in earnings reports and JDs are a signal your competitors are not pulling yet. Here is the exact play.
standalone_check: Gives a concrete, copy-paste signal idea with the extraction method and the downstream email play in one breath.
risks: Opening 'they' refers to target companies — slightly vague without prior context, though inferrable; sentence 68 has garbled phrase ('getting away' likely means 'getting ahead').
